thread_analysis.thread_summary: Shimano (contact Kazuya Takahashi) engages Allion (Yukihiro Nakano, Itsuo Sakai) for Bluetooth SIG certification of their new SW-UT600 product (BLE switch device using Nordic nRF Connect SDK v2.8.0, DIS/BS profiles), spanning March through June 2025. This is Shimano's first certification engagement since the major July 2024 registration system overhaul. The thread extensively explores returning-customer process continuity, Subset creation risk, SDK migration registration impact, hardware variance tolerance (including a clever RF PHY test reuse strategy), and RF PHY testing layer-dependency clarification.
all_questions_found: Does the placeholder model-name workaround still work under the current registration system, and is free derivative-model registration restricted to the same product category? (see thread_0057_case_01)
Is Subset creation still possible post-2024 and what reduction types are more likely to succeed? (see thread_0057_case_02)
SDK migration from S332 to nRF Connect SDK v2.8.0: does it require new registration even if supported profiles haven't changed, and how can cost be minimized? (see thread_0057_case_03)
Two products with different functions and different PCBs but the same Bluetooth IC -- how much hardware difference is tolerated, and what test validates it? (see thread_0057_case_04)
RF PHY testing across SDK/firmware changes: does a Host-layer-only change require re-testing, and how can an existing RF PHY report be reused in a new registration? (see thread_0057_case_05)

(Administrative, not separately cased) Standard pre-registration questionnaire items (SDK version, supported profiles, TX power, PTS plans), Shimano's timeline (registration completion by July 10, 2025, new model public disclosure October 10, 2025), test lab scheduling and resource availability (Japan vs Taiwan facilities, equipment calibration windows).
thread_analysis.key_technical_discussion: This thread is exceptionally rich in practical, returning-customer guidance covering the entire post-2024 landscape. Case_05's RF PHY layer-dependency insight (RF PHY only exercises HCI and below, making Host-layer firmware changes invisible to RF testing) combined with the registration-structuring strategy (reusing an existing full RF PHY report by defining the new registration around the hardware-identical product) represents a sophisticated cost-optimization technique that wouldn't emerge from the standard case-by-case approach. Cases 01-04 collectively address the major returning-customer uncertainties: whether previous workarounds still apply (yes, with caveats), whether Subset rejection risk has increased (yes), what triggers re-registration (ICS/Core-version changes, not profile-level changes), and how much hardware variation is acceptable (minor RF front-end variance is OK if validated via 2-item confirmatory test).
thread_analysis.key_decision_logic: See individual case files for case-specific logic; overarching theme is: returning customers should confirm that many pre-2024 flexibilities (placeholder names, cross-category derivatives, Subset creation) remain available, but Consistency Check is now stricter, SDK migrations have registration impact determined by ICS/Core-version change not profile change, hardware variance requires validation, and RF PHY report reuse is possible if registration structure is carefully designed around hardware identity rather than model chronology.
thread_analysis.risk_if_done_wrong: A returning customer who assumes all their previous strategies were eliminated by the 2024 overhaul could unnecessarily restrict their registration approach; conversely, assuming no changes to process or risk profile could result in unexpected test requirement increases (Subset creation failure, SDK migration re-registration, hardware variance validation gaps, or missed RF PHY report reuse opportunities).
thread_analysis.consulting_takeaway: When engaging a returning customer for their first post-2024 registration, proactively confirm continuity of pre-2024 flexibilities while clearly explaining what CHANGED (Consistency Check stringency, QDID/ICS evaluation focus, hardware variance validation requirements) and what DIDN'T change (placeholder naming, cross-category derivatives, Subset-creation capability as a system feature). Offer sophisticated cost-minimization strategies like RF PHY report reuse and SDK-migration alignment with concurrent new registrations.
